sections.title: The War of the Ring
sections.intro: A scripted war between the Free Peoples and the Shadow that grows across the campaign, with its own score, events and hunters.

cards.title: The War Begins
cards.summary: Middle-earth starts at peace and slides into the War of the Ring on a set timetable. No kingdom starts other wars before it.
points: Day 30: Isengard and Dunland attack Rohan
Day 44: every hostile kingdom goes to war, and the two sides can no longer make peace
Both start days can be changed in Mod Options

public.summary: Middle-earth starts at peace and slides into the War of the Ring on a set timetable.

cards.title: War Momentum
cards.summary: Battles, sieges, raids, armies and overall strength move a Good-versus-Evil score, shown as a slider on the campaign map. Click it for the full breakdown.
points: Events you take part in count 1.5 times as much
The war is endless by default: momentum is tracked, but nobody wins
Turn on Victory and a side wins at a 500-point lead, after you have fought in at least 5 momentum events

cards.title: The Eye of Sauron
cards.summary: Great deeds against the enemy draw a hunter after you. A Free player is hunted by one of the Nine with a host of Mordor (or of Dol Guldur). A player of the Shadow is hunted by Glorfindel with a host of the Eldar.
points: Deeds score points: a field victory, raid or forced levy 1, a sally or battle outside a siege 2, a siege assault 3
At 10 points a hunt begins; points halve every 30 days
The hunter's host is filled to 1.3 times your strength (up to 250 men) and moves faster than you once it is close
A hunt lasts up to 20 days, then there is a 60-day rest before the next

cards.title: The War Chronicle
cards.summary: Lore events of the War of the Ring happen at set points. The great sieges (Helm's Deep, Osgiliath, Minas Tirith and others) open as timed windows, and their outcome gives both sides small, temporary effects.
points: A popup on the campaign map announces each event and siege
During a siege window, armies are more eager to attack or defend that place

cards.title: Rally
cards.summary: A kingdom that has lost a large share of its towns and castles gets a small, temporary boost so the war does not end in a one-sided collapse.
points: Its towns, castles and villages fill recruit slots faster and promote waiting recruits sooner
Its captured lords escape faster
War Effect Strength scales every catch-up effect (0 turns them off)

cards.title: Fire and Tribute
cards.summary: Once the war is in full swing, raiding hosts ride out of their homelands to burn the villages of the other side.
points: Shadow: the hosts of Gundabad, Rhûn, Harad and Dunland, and the Blacklocks of Erebor
Free Peoples: the outlaw bands of Gondor and Mirkwood
Neutral: the Corsair Host of Umbar rides against either side
If your clan owns villages, a host sends an envoy asking for gold; the price grows with each envoy you seize

sections.title: Strategy, AI and Alignment
sections.intro: AI kingdoms that follow a plan, and a world split between the Free Peoples and the Shadow.

cards.title: AI Strategic Intelligence
cards.summary: In the base game an army re-scores every target every 3 hours and abandons its march the moment another town scores slightly higher. TAOM gives armies a plan.
points: Commitment: once an army picks a siege target, another target must score 4 times better before it turns away
Priority lists: each major realm pushes toward its lore objectives in order, such as Mordor to East Osgiliath, West Osgiliath, Minas Tirith, then Pelargir, or Isengard to Helm's Deep, then Edoras
Aggression: evil realms besiege at even strength instead of waiting for a 2-to-1 advantage
Reach: far-off priority targets stay on the table on TAOM's large map
War theaters: kingdoms favour enemies on their own front (Gondor prefers Mordor and Isengard over far northern targets)
Home defence counts more than in the base game

cards.title: Free Peoples and the Shadow
cards.summary: Every realm and culture is Free, Evil or Neutral, and that line shapes who fights, marries and serves together.
points: No recruiting volunteers in a settlement held by the other side
No marriages across the line; Neutral cultures (Khand, Umbar, Shaghâna, Âbanissa) marry anyone
Wanderers will not serve a player from the other side
Troops of the other side desert a party or garrison, half of each type per day
Recruiting prisoners of your own side costs no morale
Free and Evil tournaments do not seat each other's fighters
No recruiting volunteers in a settlement held by the other side
No marriages across the line; Neutral cultures (Umbar, Shaghâna, Âbanissa and Dunland) marry anyone
Wanderers will not serve a player from the other side
Troops of the other side desert a party or garrison, half of each type per day
Recruiting prisoners of your own side costs no morale

cards.title: Fair Fief Grants
cards.summary: Captured towns and castles go to the clans that fought for them, not automatically to the king's own clan.
points: The clan that carried the assault gets 2.5 times the claim; clans that were absent get half
Landless clans are favoured, and each fief a clan already holds weakens its next claim
Clans of the settlement's culture are favoured, so an orc clan rarely ends up holding an elven city
A king holding more than a third of the realm's fiefs can no longer overrule the council

cards.title: Lords Hold Their Hosts
cards.summary: AI lords keep the large armies they spawn with instead of being trimmed back to the base game's 50 to 150 men within a day.
points: Optional multipliers for lord parties and garrisons (neutral by default)
Optional food and wage relief for very large AI parties

cards.title: Siege Defence Events
cards.summary: When a watched realm's settlement is besieged, you get 3 days to ride to its defence.

cards.title: Sieges and Marches
cards.summary: Campaign rules that make sieges and movement feel like war.
points: Lords stop fleeing a siege when they are at least half as strong as the whole siege camp
An enemy castle or town with 30 or more troops harasses lords marching close to its walls, slowing them
You can call parties into your army while you lead a siege
Free armies hold a captured fort for about a day instead of leaving at once

sections.title: Your Path
sections.intro: Who you are in Middle-earth: a career, a soldier in someone else's host, or a lord who already rules.

cards.title: Careers
cards.summary: Every hero can take a career, a Middle-earth class with its own play style. There are 70 careers, about three for each realm, from the Ranger of Ithilien to the Corsair Captain and the Olog-hai Warchief.
points: Always-on passive bonuses (wages, party size, speed, morale, troop costs and more)
An active battle ability on the V key: a buff for you and nearby allies, shaped by your role (infantry, ranged or cavalry)
A three-tier choice tree; tiers open with your level
Lore rank titles, such as Ithilien Scout, Ranger of Ithilien, then Captain of the White Company
Chosen at character creation, where it also sets your starting gear; switch later by talking to a companion

public.summary: Every hero can take a career, a Middle-earth class with its own play style. There are 67 careers, about three for each realm, from the Ranger of Ithilien to the Corsair Captain and the Olog-hai Warchief.

cards.title: Career Quests
cards.summary: A career tier can come with a quest. Finishing it opens that tier of your choice tree early and gives a reward. Questing is a shortcut, never a blocker: levelling still opens every tier.
points: Objectives: win battles or tournaments, capture settlements, defeat lords, visit places, reach skill, renown or gold goals
Rewards: an early tier, renown, influence or an item
Quests are offered as a prompt; turn one down and it will not ask again
More careers are getting quests over time

cards.title: Enlistment
cards.summary: Swear an oath to a lord and serve in his column as a common soldier. Your own party marches with you, out of sight, and is handed back when your service ends.
points: A term of 365 days; wages of 5, 8, 14 and 22 a day by rank, paid from the lord's own purse
Climb from Recruit to Soldier, Veteran and Sergeant
Choose infantry, archer, cavalry or support; each battle is scored 0 to 100 on how well you fought that role
13 field duties, 11 camp duties and 3 camp incidents, offered by what the column is doing
Draw your own realm's service kit from the quartermaster at each rank
Leave with honour after your term; desert early and you lose your back pay

cards.title: Battlefield Promotions
cards.summary: Soldiers who do the killing in a hard fight can be raised into named companions, keeping the gear they fought in and skills that fit their level.
points: Only battles where you were not heavily outnumbering the enemy count
Each kill banks merit for that troop type; at 32 merit a promotion is offered
Name them, or keep the name they carried into battle
Only humans, dwarves and elves can be promoted; your companion limit is respected
Paused while you are enlisted

cards.title: Play as an Existing Lord
cards.summary: At character creation, pick a lord of your culture and play the campaign as him: his face, gear, skills, clan, fiefs and kingdom, and his throne if he has one.
points: Lists the ruling house, the clan leaders and the wanderers of your culture
Click a lord to preview him; click again to get your own character back
A wanderer joins your own named clan instead, under the banner you designed
The backstory questions are skipped; your career choice carries over
Sauron and the Nazgûl can be unlocked, but a player-controlled dark lord can be captured

cards.title: Themed Character Creation
cards.summary: Kysaro's faction screen with painted portraits, a map and a hero picker, plus reskinned face, backstory, banner, naming and options screens.
points: Each screen can be switched back to the base game's look in Mod Options

sections.title: Armies and Recruitment
sections.intro: Elite troops cost more than gold, and armies grow out of the land they hold.

cards.title: Troop Weight
cards.summary: In the base game every soldier takes one party slot. In TAOM powerful units take more, so you cannot field an army of nothing but legends. Evil realms lean on numbers, good realms on quality.
points: Elites take 2 slots, the highest elites (level 41 and up) 3
Warg riders 2, cave trolls 4, mûmakil 10
Your party count shows the weighted total everywhere you see it
AI lords obey the same limit and shed their weakest troops when they upgrade
Weight limits how many elites you field, not how well they fight

cards.title: Special Resources
cards.summary: Every realm has a second war currency next to gold and influence, needed to field and keep its elite troops. Realms in the same group share one balance.
points: Earned from battles, raids, sieges, prisoners, tournaments, hideouts and a little every day per town; each realm earns in its own way
Spent to buy elites, to upgrade into them, and as daily upkeep
At 0, a tenth of each upkeep troop type deserts per day (with a warning a day ahead)
Your balance and a breakdown are on the map bar
The full tables are below

cards.title: The Elite Emissary
cards.summary: At each realm's capital, an emissary sells that realm's elite troops for its special resource. Conquer the capital and the offer changes to the new owner's troops.
points: The towns and prices are in the tables below

cards.title: Castle Recruitment
cards.summary: Castles get three notables with volunteers, so you can recruit at any castle you can enter. AI lords recruit there too.

cards.title: Culture Conversion
cards.summary: A conquered town or castle, with its villages, takes on the new owner's culture: its troops, militia and identity.
points: Converts one day after capture by default
Notables are replaced by ones of the new culture (a Mordor-held Gondor town gets orc notables)
The garrison is re-manned with the new culture's troops of the same tier and role
Your own hand-picked garrisons can be left alone
Converts one day after capture by default
Notables are replaced by ones of the new culture (a Mordor-held Gondor town gets orc notables)

cards.title: Supply Lines
cards.summary: Order supply convoys from a town, castle or friendly lord: goods from real market stock and troops from volunteers, delivered to you on the map.
points: A small markup and a delivery fee by distance
Hire a mercenary escort for dangerous roads

cards.title: Armour Acquisition
cards.summary: Light and medium armour is easy to find. Heavy, elite and lord armour is sold only where a town's armoury (its Barracks) is high enough.
points: Lord kit can be forged there or earned piece by piece
Beating an enemy lord can rarely drop his household's harness
Now and then a master armourer visits a town for a week and raises its armoury

cards.title: Quartermaster Orders
cards.summary: Name a companion Quartermaster and give standing orders: buy food in markets, slaughter livestock when stores run low, and raise spirits with pay or drink.
points: The food order never spends the gold needed for your next 3 days of wages

cards.title: Camps and Refuges
cards.summary: Pitch field or fortified camps on the campaign map for morale and foraging, or set ambushes and lookouts. Raise a camp into a refuge: a lasting base with a garrison and stores.
points: Up to 3 refuges, depending on clan tier; upgrade one into a stronghold
Defenders of a refuge take 20% less damage (35% in a stronghold), and militia rally to it under attack

sections.title: Battle
sections.intro: Each race and culture fights its own way, and big creatures hit like big creatures.

cards.title: Combat Mechanics
cards.summary: A pack of combat rules that make weight, skill and size matter.
points: A much more skilled fighter can crush through a block with a strong swing
Troll, mûmak, elephant and giant spider attacks can only be blocked with a shield
Orc and Uruk swings can break through shield blocks, so turtling against a horde is no longer safe
Troll and mûmak swings cleave through several soldiers; big creatures shrug off small hits
Charges knock down by weight: a mûmak bowls over infantry, a horse cannot floor a troll, dwarves stand their ground
Cavalry charge damage by culture: elves 1.6×, Rohan 1.5×, Rhûn 1.4×, Gondor 1.3×, Dale and the orc realms 1.2×
A much more skilled fighter can crush through a block with a strong swing
Troll, mûmak, elephant and giant spider attacks can only be blocked with a shield
Orc and Uruk swings can break through shield blocks, so turtling against a horde is no longer safe
Troll and mûmak swings cleave through several soldiers; big creatures shrug off small hits
Charges knock down by weight: a mûmak bowls over infantry, a horse cannot floor a troll, dwarves stand their ground

cards.title: Race Abilities
cards.summary: AI soldiers use a battle ability of their race (or, for men, their culture) when the moment comes, and nearby kin join in.
points: Berserkers go berserk when hurt; Uruk-hai fall into bloodlust on a kill; dwarves stand fast
War cries in each race's own voice
Coloured outlines show an active ability: red for fury, steel blue for a guard, violet for dread

cards.title: Culture Battle Styles
cards.summary: Each culture holds under fear and fights in melee its own way.
points: Dwarves, Elves, Isengard, Gundabad and Dol Guldur never rout
Orcs attack on sight and rarely cover; Dwarves and Gondor raise shields and hold; Elves shoot straighter; Rohan commits to a charge from further out
Optional culture doctrines for whole battles (off by default): Dwarves hold a shield wall on high ground, Elves ring their archers with infantry, Rohan leads with cavalry

cards.title: Hammerhand and Horse Stand
cards.summary: Two more battle changes.
points: A shield bash or kick can knock a man down
Outnumbered against horse, Dwarves, Isengard and Dale find ground cavalry cannot ride over

cards.title: Sauron and the Nine
cards.summary: The dark lords fight like no one else on the field.
points: Aura of Dread: enemy troops near a Nazgûl or Sauron lose morale and break sooner (the aura alone never routs anyone)
Signature strikes: Sauron's overhead Slam floors the target and knocks down everyone around it; the Nine have a Scream
Sauron and the Nazgûl cannot be captured: beaten, they flee and return with a new army within days
Aura of Dread: enemy troops that stay close to a Nazgûl or Sauron lose morale until their formation breaks
Sauron and the Nazgûl cannot be captured: beaten, they flee and return with a new army within days

cards.title: Fell Foes
cards.summary: Small changes that make the end of a battle less tidy.
points: A cornered enemy who has just been hit turns and fights instead of running
Idle enemy archers in range may pick you as their target
When only a few enemy stragglers are left, they leave the field so the battle ends and they can be taken prisoner

cards.title: Sieges
cards.summary: Choose who fights before a wall battle, and creatures that make sense in a siege.
points: Before an assault or a defence, pick your troops on the Manage Troops screen; trolls start unticked
Trolls stay off ladders and towers: attacking trolls break the gate, defending trolls hold the ground behind it
Your horse goes to your inventory for a siege and comes back afterwards

public.title: Siege Dismount
public.summary: Your horse goes to your inventory for a siege and comes back afterwards.

cards.title: Mixed Formations
cards.summary: Formations with both melee and ranged troops arrange themselves: infantry in front and archers behind by default.
points: Press L to cycle a formation through four layouts: infantry front, ranged front, ranged on the wings, or checkerboard

cards.title: Fairer Auto-Resolve
cards.summary: Auto-resolved battles know about TAOM's tier 7 to 10 troops, and each culture has its own survival rate.
points: Wounded survive more often in Gondor (+30%) and Lothlórien (+50%) armies, and less often in Mordor's (-20%)

cards.title: Smoother Big Battles
cards.summary: Fallen soldiers fade after a minute and a battle keeps at most 25 bodies; dead mounts are removed after 5 seconds. This keeps big battles, cavalry battles above all, running smoothly.
points: On the first start, the game offers to lower your ragdoll and corpse settings if they are high

public.summary: Dead mounts are removed 5 seconds after they fall, which keeps cavalry battles running smoothly.

sections.title: Creatures
sections.intro: TAOM's beasts are not ridden horses: each runs its own small AI that decides, many times a second, what to do next.

cards.title: Wargs
cards.summary: Warg mounts of Gundabad, Dol Guldur and Isengard attack nearby enemies on their own with their bite, without any rider input.
points: Hurt badly enough, a warg flies into a rage and takes over from its rider to go after whatever wounded it

cards.title: Giant Spiders
cards.summary: The Dol Guldur spider picks its strike by where its target stands: a pounce straight ahead, or a leg swipe to the left or right. Its bites are deadly and can crit.
points: Spider Riders can climb to brown and pale spiders on the party screen

cards.title: War Elephants and Mûmakil
cards.summary: Harad's elephant tramples what is in front of it and swings its tusks at enemies to the side. Riders fight from a howdah on its back, and the mûmak carries a war tower.
points: A mûmak takes 10 party slots and costs War Drums to buy and to feed
Both are bought from the emissary at Korb Taskral
A mûmak takes 10 party slots and costs War Drums to recruit and to feed
The elephant is bought from the emissary at Korb Taskral; the mûmak joins as a volunteer

cards.title: Trolls
cards.summary: Cave and hill trolls tower over the field, shrug off small hits and cleave through lines.
points: They cost their realm's special resource to recruit from prisoners and to keep
In sieges they break gates instead of climbing ladders

cards.title: Wild Creatures
cards.summary: Spider broods spawn around Mirkwood and Dol Guldur, and wild troll bands of two to four roam near every kingdom's lands. Trolls are never taken prisoner or recruited.

sections.title: Lords and Relations
sections.intro: Friendships are earned in the field and kept with the person, not the clan.

cards.title: Personal Relations
cards.summary: Your relation with a lord stays with that lord instead of passing to his clan leader. A friendship with Faramir is not a friendship with Denethor.
points: Paying influence to disband another lord's army costs you relation with its leader

cards.title: Bonds of Battle
cards.summary: Relation is earned on campaign: fighting beside a lord, clearing bandits near a settlement, handing a lord troops, and overpaying in a barter.

cards.title: Tokens of Esteem
cards.summary: Say "I have a gift for you" to a companion or a lord and give goods from your inventory, or a purse of gold to a companion, to win relation.
points: The same hero takes no other gift for a while
Lords of the Free realms refuse gifts from a player of the Shadow

cards.title: Good Deeds and Long Memory
cards.summary: Releasing a captured lord, handing a hero prisoner to a settlement and winning a tournament earn relation. Raiding a village or forcing it to give goods costs relation with its owner and notables.
points: Rewards and costs depend on whose side each person is on
Handing a Mordor captive to Minas Tirith is worth double; raiding the enemy's villages is expected and costs little

cards.title: Captured Lords
cards.summary: A lord held in your party or dungeon can be questioned about his realm's lands, for a bribe or by force, and stripped of his gear. Or ask him to swear to your kingdom instead of being ransomed.

cards.title: Messengers
cards.summary: Send a paid messenger (50 gold) from the encyclopedia to any hero you have already met. It travels for a few days, can be ambushed, and starts a conversation when it arrives.

cards.title: Messengers to Anyone
cards.summary: Messengers can reach any hero, met or not. The price grows with distance, and is higher for strangers, enemies and besieged places.

cards.title: Smaller Touches
cards.summary: A few more ways to deal with lords, companions and the lists.
points: Gift troops to a friendly lord through a donate screen
Ask a lord who knows you where his clan's lands are, and see them on your map
Mercenary clans stay with a kingdom for a minimum number of days
On the clan screen, unhappy companions are tinted red before they leave
For a small fee, the arena master names the nearest towns holding a tournament now

sections.title: Fiefs and Economy
sections.intro: Running a realm without riding back to every town.

cards.title: Fief Management
cards.summary: Manage every fief you own from anywhere: press F6 or use the Fiefs button on the map bar to queue buildings.

public.summary: Manage every fief you own from anywhere: press F6 to queue buildings.

cards.title: Rule Your Lands
cards.summary: More things to do with the fiefs you hold.
points: Namegiving: the ruler can rename towns, castles and villages for influence
Watch-Silver: pay a governor's watch to raise a fief's loyalty
Castle patrols: a castle with a Guard House fields a patrol, as towns do
From the Ashes: rebuild a looted village of your realm, or lend your men's labour to a building project
Reeve's Ledger: the town window shows the fief's profit with a daily breakdown and its patrol, with one-click reserve buttons
Postern Gate: a building that cuts the troops lost breaking into or out of a siege

cards.title: Markets and Caravans
cards.summary: Town markets refill their gold toward a higher target (25,000 instead of 10,000), so drained markets recover. Caravans travel further, trade across the endless war and carry fuller loads.
points: Garrison food is corrected so elite garrisons do not starve their towns

cards.title: Tournaments
cards.summary: No betting limit by default, and tournaments of the Free Peoples and the Shadow do not seat each other's fighters.

sections.title: Map and Interface
sections.intro: A campaign map that reads like an atlas, and fewer clicks everywhere else.

cards.title: Realm Borders
cards.summary: Each kingdom's border is drawn on the campaign map, following rivers, coasts and mountains, and redrawn when a fief changes hands.
points: A watercolour wash in each realm's colour, with realm names when zoomed out
Your own realm's frontier is a gold cord
Zoom all the way out and a parchment map of Middle-earth fades in
A notice when you ride into another kingdom; press M to hide or show the borders

cards.title: Hidden Hosts
cards.summary: Other parties' troop counts blur with distance ("1??", then "12?", then exact) and sharpen with Scouting. Under trees, your own sight is shorter.

cards.title: Campaign Map
cards.summary: Small changes that make the large map easier to read.
points: Settlement names fade with distance and are tinted by your relation: green for yours, red for enemies, blue for allies
Party figures are half the base game's size, so settlements stand out
Faster time controls: fast-forward 4×, extra fast-forward 8×, and 16× while holding Ctrl

cards.title: Inventory and Character
cards.summary: Faster inventory work and clearer character screens.
points: Sell All opens a menu: sell damaged items, low-value items and more
A search box in the inventory
Save up to 10 equipment presets per hero
Companion roles ([BOW], [INF] and so on) on the party and battle-order screens
The encyclopedia shows every character from the start

cards.title: Better Items and Skill Limits
cards.summary: Small additions to the inventory and character screens.
points: Items that beat the selected character's gear are tinted green (upgrade) or yellow (sidegrade), with a "show only better items" filter
The character screen marks the level where each skill starts learning at its slowest

cards.title: The Look of Middle-earth
cards.summary: Kysaro's Middle-earth main menu with a Sauron video, painted loading screens and themed skill icons.
points: A main-menu option pre-compiles shaders so the first battles stutter less

sections.title: The World
sections.intro: Middle-earth itself, and playing it with friends.

cards.title: Bandits That Grow With You
cards.summary: Hideouts, bandit parties and hideout fights grow as your campaign advances, up to about 2.5 times the base game by the endgame. TAOM has 8 bandit factions.
points: A hideout boss stands with 4 bodyguards in the final fight

cards.title: Races
cards.summary: Dwarves, elves, orcs, Uruk-hai, goblins, trolls and more, each with their own size, animations, voices and combat traits.
points: The camera sits at a dwarf's eye height when you play one

cards.title: Co-op
cards.summary: TAOM works with the Bannerlord Coop and Bannerlord Together mods (one or the other, never both). The TAOM team does not provide co-op support.
points: Every player needs the same TAOM version, mod list and Mod Options settings
StoryMode must be on and War Sails off; Coop goes last in the load order
Host-a-game only: a dedicated server does not work
In co-op the host controls time, and TAOM's diplomacy rules stand down
